newsitem.title: UK: Expectations of wide EMU little changed - JP Morgan.
newsitem.headline: Expectations of wide EMU little changed - JP Morgan.

text.p: Expectations of a broad-based start to European economic and monetary union (EMU) were little changed this week even as developments in France and Germany increased perceptions of a wider, softer euro, prices monitored by JP Morgan showed Friday.

The perceived EMU probability in Sweden - which announced this week it would not join EMU from the start - drifted slightly lower to 61 percent while Spain's chances as assumed by markets firmed a touch to 77 percent from 75 last week.

The JP Morgan "EMU" calculator, derived primarily from the interest-rate swaps market, showed the probability of France and Germany founding the single currency on the planned January 1, 1999 start date unchanged at 100 percent.
The implied probability of Belgium joining EMU from the start returned to 100 percent from 96 last week.
Overall, however, expectations that other EMU hopefuls will join Germany and France from the start were little changed.

This was despite an unsettling week for markets after a surprise win for France's Socialists in parliamentary elections, and as a row between the German government and its central bank over plans to revalue the Bundesbank's gold reserves stoked fears of a wider and softer euro from the start.

Analysts said attempts by Bonn, later shelved, to revalue Bundesbank's gold reserves, in a move which would have helped it meet EMU entry criteria, would make it hard for Germany to rebuff requests from France to include EMU hopefuls Italy and Spain from the start - thus watering down the prospects for the Euro.
While expectations of a broadbased start to EMU were mainly steady, according to the JP Morgan calculator, the majority of EMU hopefuls saw chances down a touch.
Britain and Denmark saw a drop in assumptions to 45 percent from 48 percent and 50 percent, respectively.
Ireland, however, saw the largest slip as implied expectations eased to 54 percent from 73 percent last week while chances of Italy joining in the first wave remained steady at 58 percent.
Chances for Portugal, were also steady at 79 percent in the week.
JP Morgan points out there is a reasonable margin of error in overall probability levels of between three and five points.
The probabilities are derived from the actual swap spread, an in-house assumption of what the spread would be if EMU was not a factor, and the expected spread after EMU participation, which is zero.
